cases.prompt: A concentration sensor reports C(t)=C₀e^(−kt) after washout. Explain how a semilog plot estimates k, identify the units of k, and state one reason measured points may deviate from a straight line.

rubric.criterion: Takes ln(C/C₀)=−kt and identifies slope −k
States k has inverse-time units
Names a plausible model or measurement limitation such as background offset, multiple compartments, sensor lag, or non-first-order clearance

limitations: This preserved three-criterion checklist is self-assessment, not an analytic grading rubric or an institutional grade.

cases.prompt: Washout project milestone 1 (suggested week 12). For the project's corrected signal S(t) = 18e^(−0.08t) + 6e^(−0.015t), derive S′ and S″, find the initial rate of change, show that S decreases on [0, 24] and use the sign of S″ to locate the steepest decline.

rubric.criterion: I differentiated each exponential term and kept the units signal units per hour.
I showed that every term of S′ is negative, so S decreases on the whole interval.
I used the sign of S″ to explain where the decline is steepest.
I checked my method on the open rehearsal before using the project model.

limitations: Optional self-check for the washout-model project. The response is saved privately and is never submitted, scored or graded; the separate inactive project draft and its proposed rubric remain unreviewed.

cases.prompt: Washout project milestone 2 (suggested week 12). Find when the corrected signal first reaches 8 units: establish a unique root on [20, 24], apply Newton's method to f(t) = S(t) − 8 from t₀ = 20 h for at least two iterations, and substitute the final estimate back into f.

rubric.criterion: I showed a sign change on [20, 24] and used S′ < 0 to argue the root is unique.
I wrote each Newton update with f and f′ evaluated at the previous estimate.
I kept enough digits between steps and reported the residual of the final estimate.
